newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire hosts Southern Africa electricity meeting.
newsitem.headline: Zaire hosts Southern Africa electricity meeting.

text.p: Zaire, which has huge hydro-electric potential, is host to a meeting of Southern African countries designed to boost cooperation in electricity production and supply.

Zaire's deputy minister for energy, Omer Tumba, told the opening session of the Southern African Power Pool meeting on Monday that electricity played an important in trading relations between African countries.
"Control of energy is a determining factor in development. Connection between the national grids is becoming the cement in integration of African countries," he said.

The gathering, which groups representatives from Zaire, South Africa, Botswana, Malawi, Mozambique, Namibia, Swaziland, Zambia and Zimbabwe, ends on Thursday. Tanzania and Lesotho did not send delegates.
The minister estimated Zaire's generating potential, based on rivers across the sprawling Central African country but particularly on the lower reaches of the Zaire River, was 100,000 megawatts.
He said that the giant Inga hydroelectric complex alone already offered huge potential supplies for the region.
Zaire's state power company has been a member of the group since 1994.
